quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: On slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains, snows, or sleets. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: To turn left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from which lane?
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need extra effort to steer. Reduce speed and pull off the road to stop safely.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully steer back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed without hard braking and carefully steer back onto the road. Check for other traffic before re-entering the road.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What can you do from a center turn lane?
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is for left turns only. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: A train is close and moving fast. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route around the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train completely passes before crossing.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast, do not cross. This is true even if signals are broken or missing.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that parking is not allowed. It is a regulation sign that shows rules drivers must follow.

questions.question: What can help you sober up after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, exercise, or eating may make you feel more alert, but they do not speed up how fast alcohol leaves your system.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in their driveways with their cars running.

questions.explanation: Quick stops use fuel because your car must accelerate again to reach traffic speed. Look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
questions.explanation: To handle dangerous situations, you must see and identify problems early. Look far ahead, but also scan the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: You can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if the other vehicle is turning left and a passing lane is available. You may also pass on the right on multi-lane roads with two or more lanes in your direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn you about construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your car slow before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops are dangerous. Release the gas pedal first to slow your car. Then press the brake pedal smoothly. This lights up your brake lights and gives drivers behind you time to react.

questions.question: You must be extra careful when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to prevent hitting the pedestrian.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers of your plan.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like cars and trucks.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block traffic. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If you are driving behind a motorcycle, your following distance should be at least:
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. If the motorcycle and rider fall, you need extra distance to stop and avoid them.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better

questions.explanation: Fog reduces your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive carefully and slow down. Do not use high beam headlights. Use low beams instead — they light up the road and objects better in fog.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate lanes moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the middle of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
